wrap.summary: The week was dominated by the Jalen Hurts news and a run of unbeaten teams. The Raiders lost their third straight game, and Kansas City, Minnesota and San Francisco are still undefeated.

storylines.text: Hurts is expected to miss the season with blood clots, and the NFL has concluded the Eagles handled his clearance appropriately.
The Chiefs, Vikings and 49ers are unbeaten. Kansas City beat the Chargers 22–6, and San Francisco beat the Commanders 23–17.

headlines.title: Jalen Hurts expected to miss the season with blood clots
headlines.summary: Sources told NFL Network and ESPN that doctors found multiple blood clots in Hurts' lungs. The Eagles and his agent say he has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, and that he is clinically stable with no significant functional limitations. Treatment with blood thinners is expected to continue. The NFL has reportedly concluded the process that cleared him for Week 5 was handled appropriately, and the Eagles will not be punished.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Eagles are 2–4 and have lost four straight, so their quarterback situation for the rest of the season now matters most.

headlines.title: Rams go through another kicker after Blake Grupe's ACL tear
headlines.summary: Grupe tore his ACL while trying to make a tackle in the Rams' 18–16 loss to the Cardinals. He had replaced Harrison Mevis, who missed a 50-yard field goal and had a 48-yarder blocked in overtime of a Week 5 loss to the Bills, and was cut a day later. The Rams worked out Brandon McManus and Matt Prater on Tuesday and are signing McManus, who is 35. He made 24 of 30 field goals for the Packers last season. The same week, Davante Adams (hamstring) was ruled out for six to 10 weeks and Kobie Turner (groin) for four to six weeks, and Poona Ford is out for the season.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Rams are 2–4 and have a long list of injuries to work through. They play the Raiders in Week 7.

headlines.title: NFL to boost security for Steelers-Saints game in Paris
headlines.summary: The NFL says security will be heightened for the Steelers and Saints game in Paris after civil unrest in the French capital last weekend. League executive Peter O'Reilly said officials have been in Paris for about 10 days working on logistics. He said the league has never been close to moving its first game in France. The Steelers are 4–2 and the Saints are 2–4.
headlines.whyItMatters: It is the league's first game in France, and the Steelers and Saints play it on October 25.

headlines.title: Patriots lose Romeo Doubs to injured reserve
headlines.summary: Doubs landed hard on his right shoulder after a diving 42-yard touchdown catch in the Patriots' 26–19 win over the Jets. He has been placed on injured reserve and will miss at least four games, starting Thursday night at Chicago. He has 14 catches for 261 yards and three touchdowns this season. Morgan Moses, Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown also left that game with injuries. Drake Maye threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns.
headlines.whyItMatters: New England is 4–2 and has lost receiver and offensive line depth in the same week, while Caleb Lomu may move positions.

recaps.text: The 49ers held off the Commanders 23–17 in a one-score game, improving to 6–0. Christian McCaffrey scored twice and Brock Purdy threw for 264 yards and a touchdown, but the story was Jayden Daniels, who threw for 300 yards and two touchdowns in a loss that drops Washington to 1–4–1. Sonny Styles led the Commanders with 13 tackles. San Francisco's win keeps it well clear at the top of the NFC West, while Washington is now close to the bottom of the NFC East.

contextCard.title: How NFL international games work
contextCard.body: The NFL plays a small number of regular-season games outside the United States each year. One team is listed as the home team, and the league runs the logistics and security with the host city. Because these games are planned well ahead, a change in the host city's situation can affect the schedule.

headlines.title: AJ Dybantsa out of Wizards' opener with ankle injury
headlines.summary: The No. 1 pick will miss Wednesday's opener against the Bucks with a tweaked ankle, coach Brian Keefe said. Keefe described him as day-to-day, so he could debut this weekend. The Wizards play Toronto on Friday and go to Chicago on Saturday. Dybantsa averaged 12.8 points on 43.9% shooting in the preseason, with 18.2% from three. He is starting his rookie season alongside Trae Young and Anthony Davis, and scouts were divided about that arrangement.

headlines.title: Paul George sets Celtics debut record
headlines.summary: George scored 31 points in his first 20 minutes for Boston against Detroit. He was 10-for-14 from the floor and 6-for-8 from three, and his 31 points are a new franchise record for a Celtics debut. He arrived in the Jaylen Brown trade and is 36. Boston started Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Jayson Tatum, Paul George and Mitchell Robinson.
headlines.whyItMatters: George has played well alongside Tatum, which could keep the Celtics among the East's best if he stays healthy.

headlines.title: Hornets without Knueppel, White and Grant Williams for opener
headlines.summary: Charlotte will be without Kon Knueppel, Coby White and Grant Williams when it opens at Brooklyn on Wednesday. Knueppel missed the whole preseason with a left hamstring injury. White has a left calf strain, and Williams has a right hamstring injury. Knueppel averaged 18.5 points as a rookie and led the league with 273 made threes. The Hornets traded LaMelo Ball to Minnesota over the summer and are relying on Knueppel and White.
headlines.whyItMatters: Charlotte is counting on Knueppel and White after trading Ball, so the early absences matter more than usual.
